stores.name: Evidence certificate layer (EvidenceCertificate / SignedEvidence / PathCertificate)
stores.model: Pydantic signed cert binding finding_ref -> oracle_context_digest (sha256 of canonical oracle_context) + artifacts[] (ArtifactRef: path relative to engagement evidence root, per-file sha256, size) + engagement_slug + monotonic seq. cert_digest = sha256 of canonical bytes = the hash-chain link. SignedEvidence wraps it with m-of-n Ed25519 governance signatures + optional RFC3161 time-anchor sidecar. PathCertificate binds a derived attack path to backing_cert_digests (the finding certs it leans on). ReportClaim binds report sentences (fact vs analyst-commentary). D2 fields bind collector/scope/capture provenance. NO tenant_id field - only engagement_slug.
stores.persistence: PCF bundle written to disk by proof/bundle.py: evidence-bundle.json + trust-root.json + TRUST-ROOT-FINGERPRINT.txt + reverifiable.json, 0600, under a run/bundle dir. ChainEntry/SignedChainHead give tamper-evidence + monotonic last_seq anti-rollback. NO cert-by-id index: verify_bundle resolves certs by finding_ref from an in-memory contexts dict the caller assembles.

stores.name: Raw artifact / HTTP evidence archive (evidence_dir)
stores.model: Per-action directory of raw request/response/body bytes, each file bound by per-file sha256 into the cert's ArtifactRef manifest (manifest_dir). action_id is NOT an unguessable capability: it is a per-agent counter (A-NNN, exploit_agent.py) or a content hash poc-<sha256(check_id)[:16]> (proof/run.py). Artifact identity = (slug, action_id, relpath, sha256). verify_certificate re-hashes these from evidence_root and fails CLOSED on mismatch or when artifacts are CLAIMED but no evidence_root supplied.
stores.persistence: Filesystem under CRUCIBLE_ROOT/targets/<slug>/evidence/, 0600/0700, re-rooted onto ephemeral tmpfs for ZDR sessions. No content-addressed CAS; no global index.

stores.name: Event spine / blackboard (single source of truth)
stores.model: Append-only SQLite event log: BlackboardEventRow(id, engagement_id, kind, agent_name, payload_json, parent_id, supersedes_id) indexed by (engagement_id, kind). The signed-file variant is append-only canonical-JSON-per-line, hash-chained with vigil_core.chain, TWO Ed25519 sigs per line (record sig authenticating the snapshot + entry sig authenticating the chain-link entry_hash so delete/reorder cannot be hidden). Every projection (F4 graph, worldmodel, graph/store.py) derives from this; it is the backbone for actions/results/leads/decisions as events.
stores.persistence: SQLite (D2 tenant-sharded via paths.blackboard_dir) + append-only signed JSONL file. Rebuild re-runs Finding validator + _facts_store_is_sound so a status=fact finding with empty evidence_ref is SKIPPED even if validly signed.

stores.name: Attack-chain investigation graph (F4) + Neo4j live binder
stores.model: Typed provenance DAG: AttackChain -> ChainStep -> {ChainFinding|ChainFailure|ChainDecision} bridged to recon nodes (CVE/Host/Port/Technology/Endpoint). ConfirmationStatus split CONFIRMED (signed evidence_ref present) vs LEAD (never queryable as fact). Provenance = spine_hash (node identity) + signature_ref + evidence_ref (SCITT/OpenVEX cert id, present IFF confirmed) + engagement_id. Bi-temporal valid_from/invalid_from keyed on spine SEQUENCE; refutation retires, never deletes; LEAD->CONFIRMED is monotone. This is the closest existing thing to an evidence-linked investigation graph.
stores.persistence: In-memory GraphView per group_id (deterministically rebuilt from signed spine records; projector is the ONLY writer) + optional real Neo4j, written only by rebuild_from_spine (clear engagement partition + re-project). Reads are retrieval_only/authoritative=False (frozen).

stores.name: World-model belief / asset + attack-path graph
stores.model: Typed Node (HOST/SERVICE/ENDPOINT/WEBAPP/DATASTORE/CLOUD_RESOURCE/NETWORK_SEGMENT/PRINCIPAL/CREDENTIAL/SESSION/CONTROL/FINDING + intel kinds DOMAIN/CERTIFICATE/ASN/NETBLOCK/ORG/PACKAGE/VULNERABILITY/...) each with a Beta belief; Edge (REACHABLE_FROM/HAS_GRANT/CAN_ASSUME/VALID_ON/EVIDENCES/OWNS/HOLDS/REACHED/AFFECTS/...). classify_provenance() grades each write: cert:/evidence:/finding:/oracle: prefixes = GROUNDED, llm/assume/demoted = UNGROUNDED. stores.name: Remediation / retest certificate layer (VF-1a)
stores.model: RemediationCertificate (vigil-remediation-cert-v2): the NEGATIVE proof-carrying artifact certifying the original exploit oracle went SILENT over the patched build's re-captured bytes. Binds original_finding_cert_digest -> the signed POSITIVE finding EvidenceCertificate, so exploitable->remediated is bound together by ID. Minted only when the oracle genuinely re-fires and does NOT confirm; Ed25519 signed; verified by re-execution (oracle silent + context digest match + sig verify vs pinned governance key). reprove.py re-proves a finding. This is the de-facto retest mechanism.
stores.persistence: Signed JSON attestation + attestation_log / ledger. Links to the finding by cert digest; not projected as a graph node/edge.

Evidence integrity/signing: m-of-n Ed25519 + trust_root fingerprint PIN (fail-closed before any sig check); cert_digest hash-chain (ChainEntry/SignedChainHead) + monotonic anti-rollback high-water; artifact sha256 re-hash fail-closed; signed spine (record + entry sigs) rejects tamper/reorder; evidence-less fact SKIPPED on rebuild/checkpoint even if validly signed

Tenant isolation: D2 shard isolates spine + memory per CRUCIBLE_TENANT; assert_tenant_fleet_isolated FAILS CLOSED unless root is dedicated per tenant; verify_bundle enforces single-engagement (reject cross-engagement mix); Neo4j MERGE/MATCH is engagement_id-scoped so a foreign partition cannot alias; _validated() rejects traversal in tenant ids

No secrets in labels/logs/exports: F3 redactor (redact_evidence / redact_tool_args, one vocabulary) scrubs certificate.summary/evidence, Detection.summary, and every Neo4j node property; private keys held only in process memory, never written to spine/log/export
gaps: NO evidence-by-ID resolver/index: there is no get(evidence_id) -> SignedEvidence + verify store API. evidence_ref is an opaque, non-uniform string (detection cert_id | spine hash | SCITT/OpenVEX id | sha256:<daa>). The graph's CONFIRMED derivation checks only that evidence_ref/signature_ref are NON-EMPTY; it NEVER dereferences and re-verifies the actual stored cert. A dangling or mismatched evidence_ref (points at nothing, or at another finding's cert) is undetected at the graph/query boundary. 'Evidence-linked' integrity is ASSUMED from the signed spine, not enforced by a join.

Evidence raw store is engagement-slug-keyed, not tenant-stamped or content-addressed: action_id is a counter or sha256(check_id) (predictable, not an unguessable capability); artifact identity = (slug, action_id, relpath, sha256) with no global CAS and no tenant_id anywhere in the evidence cert or graph node. In a SHARED CRUCIBLE_ROOT, two tenants running the same slug COMMINGLE evidence/findings/authority (documented in common/tenant.py) - a real cross-tenant commingling - so an evidence ID is cross-tenant-ambiguous unless root-per-tenant is deployed.

No first-class goal / remediation / retest ENTITY in the investigation graph: remediation+retest exist only as certificates (RemediationCertificate.original_finding_cert_digest) + reprove.py, and 'goal' only as an attack-path destination. The target chain's finding -> remediation -> retest segment is not projected as graph nodes/edges, so coverage/status (Verified Fixed / Bypassed / Risk Accepted) is not queryable.

No unified graph spanning all 9 entity types: entities are split across the evidence-cert layer, the spine, the F4 chain graph, and the worldmodel, each with a different id scheme (finding_ref vs cert_digest vs spine_hash vs node id). Nothing joins assets->goals->actions->results->leads->verification->findings->remediation->retests in one projection. 'Coverage' today = scan-surface coverage (scanner/coverage.py), NOT entity-coverage over the investigation model.

engagement_id/group_id graph partition is NOT access-controlled: isolation is a property-scoped MERGE/MATCH; a caller that names another engagement_id reads that partition. There is no store-enforced check that the caller owns the engagement - isolation relies on upstream authorization + root-per-tenant deployment.

verify_bundle single-engagement check has a KNOWN empty-slug ride-along (documented red-pen LOW, DEFERRED-INFRA): empty slugs are discarded, so an engagement_slug='' cert can ride a named bundle (defense-in-depth only, still requires a governance-signed head).

(1) The event spine (blackboard, agents/blackboard.py + live/spine_vigilcore.py) stays the single source of truth: add new SIGNED event KINDS for goal/remediation/retest so the full chain of custody remains spine-derived, replay-safe and tamper-evident. (2) The integration F4 graph (graph/model.py + live/graph_neo4j.py) is THE investigation read-model to extend - it already has the hard parts: CONFIRMED/LEAD split, bi-temporal retire-never-delete, evidence_ref provenance, engagement_id partition. Add NodeLabel {Goal, Remediation, Retest} and EdgeType {TARGETS_GOAL/SATISFIES, REMEDIATES, RETESTS/VERIFIED_FIXED}, mirroring them in the Neo4j binder's enum whitelist + engagement-scoped MERGE. (3) Reuse the worldmodel (worldmodel/models.py) for the asset substrate, the attack-path 'goal' (destination), the EVIDENCES edge, and its classify_provenance cert:/evidence:/finding: convention to TYPE evidence_ref. (4) Close the evidence-link gap WITHOUT weakening spine-trust: normalize evidence_ref to a scheme-prefixed typed ID (cert:<digest> / scitt:<id> / daa:<sha256>); add a per-engagement evidence resolver get(evidence_id)->SignedEvidence keyed off the PCF bundle; add an OPT-IN strict/verify graph mode that dereferences evidence_ref and re-runs the EXISTING verify_certificate/reverify_context before marking a node CONFIRMED (the worldmodel 'demoted:' marker, written when a recorded-confirmed proof fails to re-fire at projection, is the precedent). This preserves FACT authority by reusing the one independent verification path rather than duplicating it. A new DB is unjustified: Neo4j is already wired behind the F4 projection and the worldmodel store is file-backed and sufficient.
maps.notes:
Direct answers to the task questions.

CAN A FINDING REFERENCE A REAL STORED ARTIFACT BY ID TODAY? Yes - at the certificate layer, and it is re-verifiable. An EvidenceCertificate binds finding_ref -> artifacts[] (ArtifactRef relpath under targets/<slug>/evidence/<action_id>, by per-file sha256), and verify_certificate re-hashes those bytes from evidence_root and fails CLOSED if they are claimed-but-unchecked or altered. RemediationCertificate.original_finding_cert_digest links a remediation back to the exact positive finding cert, and PathCertificate.backing_cert_digests links an attack path to its backing findings. So finding->artifact, path->findings, and remediation->finding by-ID links are real and offline-re-verifiable. HOWEVER, at the investigation-GRAPH layer the link is a soft, opaque evidence_ref string that is never dereferenced or re-verified (no resolver, no referential-integrity join) - CONFIRMED is derived from evidence_ref merely being NON-EMPTY, trusting the signed append-only spine upstream.

IS ANY ID FORGEABLE? A FACT is not forgeable without the m-of-n governance keys: verify checks sigs + trust-root pin + sha256 artifact manifest + oracle re-fire, all fail-closed; the hash-chained signed spine rejects tamper/reorder; an evidence-less 'fact' is skipped on rebuild. The IDs themselves are predictable not secret (action_id = counter or sha256(check_id); cert_digest/cert_id = content sha256), but integrity rests on signatures + content hashes, not ID secrecy. Residual forgeability is a DANGLING/MISMATCHED evidence_ref at the graph boundary (undetected because unresolved) and the documented empty-slug bundle ride-along (LOW).

IS ANY ID CROSS-TENANT? There is NO tenant_id in the evidence cert or graph data model - only engagement_slug / engagement_id. On disk only the spine + memory are tenant-sharded (D2); evidence, findings and authority are slug-scoped, so a shared CRUCIBLE_ROOT with the same slug COMMINGLES evidence across tenants (documented real cross-tenant commingling). Genuine tenant isolation = one CRUCIBLE_ROOT per tenant, fail-closed for fleet workers via assert_tenant_fleet_isolated. Cross-ENGAGEMENT mixing is blocked at verify_bundle (single-engagement) except the empty-slug case; the graph partitions by engagement_id but does not authenticate partition ownership.

maps.notes: FACT vs LEAD vs CLEAN is a CLOSED, type-enforced set (verdict.Verdict = {FACT,LEAD,CLEAN,INCONCLUSIVE}; oracle_adapter.Outcome adds POSITIVE/UNSUPPORTED/ERROR/SKIPPED). FACT is minted ONLY by confirm_and_certify/certify_admitted after the full conjunct (oracle fires >=high-confidence over retained oracle_context + known oracle-mapped class + oracle validly confirms that class + declared==context class + provenance in {reproduced,live_redrive} + m-of-n governance signature), producing a signed EvidenceCertificate/SignedEvidence binding oracle_context_digest + artifact sha256. Everything confirmed-but-unmapped / LLM-provenanced / relabelled / unsigned is a LEAD (retained, honestly labelled). CLEAN requires a KNOWN-class applicable oracle with an observable channel that conclusively did not fire; an out-of-vocabulary class or an empty/unexamined family is UNSUPPORTED/INCONCLUSIVE, never CLEAN (compose([])->INCONCLUSIVE). Three independent re-execution gates keep this honest: verdict.admit (registry-driven, sole AdmittedVerdict constructor), veracity.firewall.admit (DEMOTE-ONLY re-execution of cited grounds, bound to the claim's subject), and verify.reverify (offline, python3 -m framework.v2 verify) -- re-used by report.grounding.admit_for_report/grade_finding and by scanner.campaign.populate_worldmodel (the universal choke that re-fires a proof before writing oracle: provenance, else demoted:). FACTs cross to the sovereign spine as INERT signed envelopes (inert_finding/finding_spool), m-of-n verified over exact bytes. A finding links to its evidence via EvidenceCertificate (oracle_context_digest, artifacts[sha256], confirmed_by, provenance, how_to_verify) and, in the graph read-model, via GraphView Provenance {spine_hash, signature_ref, evidence_ref(present<=>confirmed), engagement_id}; its oracle_context is the serialized FindingContext re-fired at verification time. Where verification/findings nodes should attach: the task's lead->verification->findings->remediation->retests spine is already 70% present as EVENTS on the blackboard (observation/hypothesis/plan/action/result/finding/critique) with parent_id/supersedes_id links and as the GraphView AttackChain->ChainStep->ChainFinding DAG, but Verification, Remediation and Retest are not yet first-class nodes and Goal/coverage/clean are not projected -- so the right move is to extend the existing spine->GraphView projector (not add a DB). WARNING (tenant isolation, load-bearing, from common/tenant.py): the D2 shard isolates ONLY .blackboard + .memory; targets/<slug>, evidence, authority and kill-switch are per-SLUG not per-tenant, so two tenants sharing one CRUCIBLE_ROOT + slug COMMINGLE findings/evidence/authorization -- ONE CRUCIBLE_ROOT PER TENANT is a hard deployment REQUIREMENT, and a multi-tenant investigation graph should additionally carry an explicit tenant_id node property + reject cross-tenant evidence IDs rather than relying on the filesystem layout alone. safety_gates: FACT-minting authority preserved: promote.py writes LEADs only (intel:promote provenance, GROUNDING_INTEL, confidence 0.5) and is doc'd 'a LEAD, never a fact'; planner/LLM cannot self-promote; spine_projector mints a CONFIRMED FINDING node ONLY with both non-empty signed evidence_ref AND signature_ref (_finding_confirmed), a bare status=fact is a LEAD; FindingPayload.critique_status 'confirmed' is RESERVED for a fired deterministic oracle; classify_provenance() is the single source of 'is this grounded'.

In-scope by construction (promote.py): host_matches_scope over parse_scope(slug) = the EXACT predicate the live per-request gate uses; built URL is round-tripped through extract_hostname so a scope-string-matching authority delimiter (evil.com#.example.com) or CIDR can't slip; categorical protected-domain floor is_hard_blocked (gov/mil/edu/IGO, default-ON, VIGIL_ALLOW_PROTECTED_DOMAINS) applied at the keystone AND re-gated fail-closed at probe time (kill-switch->entitlement->charter-scope->destructive->egress).

Append-only + tamper-evidence: blackboard SQL triggers refuse UPDATE/DELETE; spine_chain hash-linked + m-of-n governance-signed head; engagement_id bound into each digest (no cross-engagement head replay); verify fails closed on a truncated/altered/reordered/deleted log; grounded-only refutation (an unauthenticated refute cannot un-prove a proof).

Tenant isolation: per-process CRUCIBLE_TENANT shard dir for .memory/.blackboard; active_tenant() fails CLOSED on an unsafe id (no silent fallback to the shared singleton); a tenant worker can only ever name its own shard; spine digest + head slug-binding reject cross-engagement/cross-tenant reuse.

Evidence integrity/signing + no secrets in labels: seal-at-capture encrypts credential-bearing spine excerpts before they land (DEK in evidence_keys_dir OFF the spine for crypto-shred); PCF certs re-runnable, evidence-altered rejected at verify; world-model/plan-input/world JSON written owner-only via secure_write; monotonic seq (never wallclock) keeps projection deterministic/replayable.
gaps: No single traversable investigation graph: the 9 entity types live in 4+ disjoint stores (in-memory world-model/JSON, intel SQLite, blackboard SQLite, MLS SQLite, planner per-slug JSON) with NO shared ID space. Only the engagement slug STRING joins them; the SQLite stores use independent integer ids by design. You cannot query asset -> goal -> action -> result -> lead -> verification -> finding -> remediation -> retest as one path.

finding->asset link is not durable on the default path: EVIDENCES edges + FINDING nodes are produced ONLY by the opt-in worldmodel/spine_projector (P4); the durable MLS findings.surface is FREE TEXT with no asset node_id / obs_id / canonical_id FK. A confirmed finding is not durably joined to the lead/asset that produced it.

No durable goal->action->result->finding chain of custody: the spine carries plan_id/action_id/targets_hypothesis/derived_from_hypothesis as free-text handles inside payload_json, not as edges and not indexed as a traversable path; derived_from_hypothesis is even dropped when a finding is written to the MLS table.

No remediation entity: there is no store/row/edge for a remediation keyed to a finding_slug (only generated report prose and the remediation_binary ASan repair module). The investigation model's remediation node has nowhere durable to live.
No retest entity: there is no durable retest/status node linking a retest observation (Verified Fixed/Bypassed/Risk-Accepted) back to the original finding (only the human reports/retest.md).

Leads have no persisted lifecycle/state and are recomputed per run: promote.py writes ENDPOINT leads only into the in-memory world-model, which is NOT durably persisted by default — a lead's state (new->queued->verifying->confirmed/refuted) and its verification outcome are not tracked as linked nodes across runs; the scanner/VULNERABILITY/INDICATOR leads in intel_observations likewise carry no explicit lead-state or lead->verification link.

Coverage is not modeled as a graph: there is no durable representation of which in-scope assets/surfaces were probed vs skipped vs deferred joined to the asset graph; goal-tree leaf status lives only in the per-slug .planner-state.json checkpoint, disconnected from intel_entities.

Verification is an event, not a linked node: critique/critic_verdict/oracle_context exist on the spine but there is no verification node connecting a specific lead -> its verification attempt -> outcome -> the finding (or the refutation), so 'nothing found' cannot be shown as an explicit CLEAN-with-checks node tied to the asset it cleared.
maps.extend_not_rebuild: Extend the Intel durable store (memory/intel_schema.sql + intel/store.py), which shares ONE SQLite connection (memory.Store) with the MLS engagements/findings/hypotheses tables — do NOT add a new graph DB (Neo4j/Kuzu). Rationale: this store already persists a typed, provenance-tagged, Beta-belief node/edge graph with engagement_slug scoping, monotonic-seq determinism, idempotent upserts, and an append-mostly audit (intel_merge_log is already an audit-of-links); the world-model is merely its in-memory projection, so the graph's source of truth is already here. Add slug-scoped link + lifecycle tables in the SAME DB, keyed on the stable ids that already exist (obs_id, canonical_id, world-model node id '{kind}:{key}', hypothesis.handle, goal node id, finding.slug, evidence cert id): e.g. investigation_edges(engagement_slug, src_kind, src_id, edge, dst_kind, dst_id, provenance, grounding, evidence_ref, seq) to record asset->goal->action->result->lead->verification->finding edges as provenance-tagged rows; lead_state(engagement_slug, lead_id, state, verified_by, obs_id) for the lead lifecycle; remediation(engagement_slug, finding_slug, status, ...) and retest(engagement_slug, finding_slug, verdict, evidence_ref, seq) for the two missing entities. Measured scale (a few thousand nodes/edges per engagement, slug-scoped traversals) is well within SQLite recursive-CTE range, so no new engine is justified. Preserve every gate: link rows record provenance/grounding only and are INTEL-tier unless they cite a signed evidence_ref (FACT authority stays at the oracle seam); reject any src/dst id whose embedded engagement_slug/tenant differs from the row's (the slug column + per-process tenant shard already give that boundary); never write a credential/secret into a label (reuse seal-at-capture + secure_write).

DATA-FLOW of the dimension: collectors -> intel Observation (models.py, Admiralty-rated, polarity, monotonic seq) -> IntelIngest single-writer (ingest.py) does persist(intel_observations) -> project_observation onto in-memory WorldModel -> resolve entities -> persist(intel_entities/members/merge_log), all stamped engagement_slug. The drift state machine (proven-fixed / still-proven / regressed / present / inconclusive / refused) is computed only in attestation_log._derive_series and lives in the tick log; it is never reflected on the finding node. A graph query over confirmed_findings cannot distinguish never-remediated vs proven-fixed vs regressed.

The remediation ACTION (codefix/autopatch: gated clone->edit->build->PR, per-block approvals, m-of-n quorum, denials) is not durably persisted — CodeFixResult.steps are inert, 'the spine write is deferred'. No per-finding freshness/staleness surface. The honest residual is 'freshness = last cadence fire', but nothing records last-retest time per finding or flags a fixed finding whose re-proof cadence has lapsed; the graph cannot answer 'which fixed findings are overdue for re-proof'.

The continuous attestation-log default dir is per-base-dir (<base_dir>/attestation-log), not namespaced per-finding or per-tenant, and the CLI reprove drives ONE finding per run. Nothing structurally prevents two findings' monotonic tick series from being written into the same log_dir, and there is no registry of which findings have a running retest cadence.

'Verification' (the target model's distinct stage between leads and findings) is collapsed into the finding node's Provenance boolean (CONFIRMED + evidence_ref) plus out-of-graph cert re-execution; it is not a first-class node linking finding<->evidence<->oracle, so the verification artifact that a remediation's negative cert mirrors is not itself graph-addressable.
maps.notes: The remediation-retests dimension is implemented as a cryptographic, offline-re-verifiable layer that sits ALONGSIDE the F4 investigation graph, not inside it. Remediation is proven by a NEGATIVE proof-carrying artifact (remediation/remediation_cert.py, VF-1a: earned-by-silence with positive-control + liveness controls, whole-cert signed) and/or a two-oracle PCR attestation (remediation/attestation.py, VULN-GONE + BEHAVIOR-PRESERVED). RETESTS are the continuous re-proof loop (remediation/reprove.py) re-firing the retained oracle_context each cycle and appending signed four-state prove-cert ticks to the anti-rollback attestation log (remediation/attestation_log.py), yielding a drift timeline (proven-fixed/regressed/...). A remediation/retest links back to its finding purely by finding_ref/finding_id/original_*_digest foreign keys carried in each signed cert — never by a graph edge. The graph (graph/) models assets->goals->actions->results->leads->verification->findings as a spine-derived read-model and stops there; remediation and retests are present as DATA but absent as graph ENTITIES. Target-model mapping: assets=Host/Port/Technology/Endpoint/CVE bridge nodes; goals=AttackChain; actions=ChainStep; results=ChainFinding/Failure/Decision; leads=ChainFinding(LEAD); verification=CONFIRMED+evidence_ref (partial, in provenance); findings=ChainFinding(CONFIRMED); remediation & retests = out-of-graph signed certs/logs. Tenant/engagement scoping is by engagement slug/group_id/charter scope (there is no tenant_id primitive here); cross-engagement laundering is refused at the finding seam (inert_finding scope-binding, trusted_finding engagement_slug==scope). RBAC (vigil_core/rbac.role_can + OFFENSE_ACTION_PERM): DEFAULT-DENY. viewer<analyst<operator<owner cumulative perms; unmapped route/perm/role => None => 403. Owner-only (offense_authority) for host-exec/infra-provision/patch-apply/authority-mint; emergency halt is LOWEST tier (halt is the safe direction), un-halt is owner.

Categorical protected-domain floor (vigil_core/hard_guardrail.is_hard_blocked): pure, env-free, pre-charter deny of gov/mil/edu/IGO (TLD regex + unicode-dot fold + exact IGO list). Fail-safe ON; owner toggle VIGIL_ALLOW_PROTECTED_DOMAINS only governs this pre-filter — signed charter scope and egress floor stay in force regardless. Applied again at intel.promote.

Tenant isolation (common/tenant + common/paths): ONE tenant per process (crucible_root lru_cache size 1); only .blackboard + .memory are tenant-sharded; targets/<slug>, evidence, authority, <slug>.halt are per-SLUG not per-tenant => ONE CRUCIBLE_ROOT PER TENANT REQUIRED. assert_tenant_fleet_isolated fails closed unless sharded AND root dedicated (atomic os.link TOFU .tenant-owner claim; malformed claim is hard-fail never 'unclaimed').

FACT-minting authority is the oracle seam ALONE (verify/verifier.OracleVerifier.confirm): no oracle => no confirmation; absent input => non-firing, never assumed pass; verifier chooses the whole discriminator from protocol constants keyed on bug_class (never producer-supplied) — closes the byte-identical-response fake-FACT. Planner/brain is propose-only (--plan-only, executes nothing); intel.promote writes a LEAD never a fact.

Anti-trust-laundering projection rule (worldmodel/spine_projector + integration/graph/projector): graph written ONLY by project() over signed spine records (single writer, no LLM/tool direct write); CONFIRMED finding node <=> record carries non-empty signed evidence_ref AND signature_ref; belief grounded never manufactured (0.9 default, never 1.0); grounded-only refutation (an unsigned opinion can't un-prove a proof); verify=True re-executes retained proof at the STORED-projection boundary and demotes a non-reproducing finding to an UNGROUNDED node.

Claim discipline (scanner/tests/test_claim_discipline.py over docs/CLAIM-DISCIPLINE.md): every evidence branch declares fact_capable and clean_capable as SEPARATE booleans + evidence + limitation; a response_body-derived branch is clean_capable=false outright (nothing-found over an undecodable body is INCONCLUSIVE never CLEAN); shipped capability matrix must not out-claim the branch registry; absolutes banned without an adjacent limitation.

Coverage honesty (verify/coverage_oracle.py): three verdicts finding / clean(oracle RAN and did not fire) / inconclusive(sent but NO oracle adjudicated — NOT clean); signed m-of-n cert over canonical bytes with out-of-band pinned root; scope statement baked into signed bytes = reached surface, NOT surface completeness.

At-rest redaction (vigil_core/redact scrub_log_event + redact_log_message): mask secret-keyed field VALUES and header/bearer/secret= values by KEY name before any log or at-rest sink; evidence .http hashed AFTER masking. Evidence signing uses domain-separated tags (crucible-evidence-v1, etc.) so a sig under one purpose cannot replay as another.
gaps: GOALS are not a first-class entity: no GOAL node/table and no goal->action edge. The attack-tree lives as targets/<slug>/attack-tree.md (prose), the charter as EngagementAuthority.scope. The investigation graph needs a GOAL/objective node (projected from charter+attack-tree) and goal->action coverage edges, with scope still authoritative only via the signed authority, never the graph.

REMEDIATION and RETEST are entirely outside every graph: routes/PCR/reverify exist but there is no remediation or retest NODE and no finding->remediation->retest EDGE chain. This is the biggest missing slice of the target model (findings->remediation->retests). Must be added as signed, re-verifiable records (remediation-attestation domain tag already exists) — a retest node must be CONFIRMED only by an oracle RE-FIRE, mirroring the finding rule.

No lead->finding provenance edge: MLS hypotheses and findings share only engagement_id (FK), not a direct edge recording WHICH hypothesis a confirmed finding closed (or which dead_end refuted it). The chain assets->...->leads->verification->findings is broken at leads->findings. Add a hypothesis_id reference on finding (and dead_end) as a link, never as a promotion path.

No single evidence-linked graph spans all 9 entities: assets+findings live in WorldModel; actions+results+leads live as flat blackboard events and MLS rows; the integration GraphView models the chain DAG but only Chain*/Host/Port/Endpoint/CVE. The entities exist but across 4 disjoint stores with no unified, re-buildable projection. A coverage layer must be a NEW PROJECTION over the existing signed spine, not a 5th authoritative store.

Coverage is a per-scan detached certificate (coverage_oracle), not wired into the persistent graph: there are no coverage nodes/edges linking (surface,param,class,verdict) to assets/goals, so 'what was provably-tested-clean vs inconclusive vs untested' cannot be queried as graph coverage. Extend by projecting coverage_oracle verdicts as edges, preserving finding/clean/inconclusive AND the reached-surface-not-completeness scope.

TENANT COMMINGLING in the graph layer: neither WorldModel JSON snapshots (per run_dir under root) nor the integration Neo4j mirror are tenant-sharded. The Neo4j mirror partitions by engagement_id/group_id ONLY (no tenant_id on nodes), and engagement_id/slug is derived from the target — so two tenants in a shared root/shared Neo4j that scan the same target commingle exactly like targets/evidence/authority do. A new graph MUST either live under the per-tenant CRUCIBLE_ROOT or carry a tenant_id in every node key AND every query predicate; a shared Neo4j/Kuzu instance re-opens the hazard tenant.py warns about.

Cross-tenant / fabricated evidence-ID risk if the graph references bare evidence_ref strings: evidence_ref + signature_ref are per-slug and not tenant-qualified. A graph/coverage layer that renders a CONFIRMED edge from a stored evidence_ref MUST re-verify by re-execution (verify=True path already exists) and bind (tenant,slug,evidence_ref) — never trust a recorded 'confirmed' status or a bare ref, or a fabricated/cross-tenant ref could launder a fact.

Two owner ties still open (spine_domains): offense-usage-ledger and continuous-attestation-log are NOT owner-rooted. If a new graph/coverage layer signs or anchors its records, it must chain to the owner via an existing owner-rooted segment (offense-finding-anchor1 / offense-spine / crucible-blackboard-chain), not invent a new un-rooted signer.
maps.extend_not_rebuild: EXTEND two existing stores; do NOT stand up a new graph DB. (1) The durable record spine = the tenant-sharded MLS SQLite (engine/crucible/framework/v2/memory/schema.sql): add the missing entity tables/columns (goals, remediation, retests) and the missing LINK columns/tables (hypothesis_id on findings for lead->finding; finding_id on remediation; remediation_id + oracle-refire on retests), as a numbered migration (_migration_3) — it already holds engagements/findings/hypotheses/payloads/dead_ends, is tenant-sharded, FK-linked and owner-0600. (2) The typed investigation/coverage GRAPH = extend worldmodel.models (NodeKind/EdgeKind) + worldmodel.spine_projector with GOAL/ACTION/RESULT/REMEDIATION/RETEST/COVERAGE node+edge kinds, keeping it a PURE one-way projection over the signed blackboard spine (the append-only, UPDATE/DELETE-refused event log that already records observation/action/result/finding/refusal events). Reuse the integration bi-temporal pattern (invalid_from, never delete) for refute/retest retirement. Reasons a new DB is unjustified: the target model is already a typed provenance graph the WorldModel implements (classify_provenance, Beta belief, projection-only single writer, verify=True re-execution); a new shared Neo4j/Kuzu instance would REINTRODUCE the tenant-commingling the Neo4j mirror already has (engagement_id-only partition). Only recommend a dedicated graph DB if measured scale (campaign node/edge counts in docs/SCALE.md, currently ~100MB/process) exceeds the in-memory+JSON+SQLite envelope — and even then it must be instantiated per-tenant (one per CRUCIBLE_ROOT) or tenant_id-partitioned in every node key and query predicate.
maps.notes:
WHAT A NEW GRAPH/COVERAGE LAYER MUST NOT WEAKEN (the exact invariants, each already enforced in code):

1) FACT-minting stays with the oracle seam alone. The graph is a CONSUMER of facts, never a producer. A node/edge may be CONFIRMED only when the underlying spine record carries a non-empty signed evidence_ref AND signature_ref (spine_projector _finding_confirmed / integration _is_confirmed). A planner/brain/LLM write enters only as a LEAD (GROUNDING_INTEL/UNGROUNDED) — classify_provenance is the single arbiter and must not be bypassed by a new provenance prefix. Never let a coverage/graph node self-certify.

2) "Nothing found" is NEVER CLEAN without the required checks. Preserve the three-verdict honesty (finding/clean/inconclusive): clean == an applicable oracle RAN and did not fire; a surface with no adjudicating oracle, or evidence that could not be decoded, is INCONCLUSIVE. A coverage graph must carry this verdict explicitly per (surface,param,class) and must repeat coverage_oracle's baked scope note (reached surface != surface completeness). Do not let a graph render absence-of-edge as proof-of-absence.

3) Stored projections re-execute, never trust. Any node/edge built from a STORED report must go through the verify=True re-execution choke point (TRUTHENOVATION T1): a recorded-'confirmed' finding whose retained proof no longer re-fires grants NOTHING and is demoted to an UNGROUNDED node (the 'demoted:' marker). Grounded-only refutation holds — an unsigned opinion cannot un-prove a proof.

4) Evidence integrity/signing + no fabricated/cross-tenant IDs. Bind every evidence reference to (tenant, slug, evidence_ref) and re-verify the signed bytes; reject a bare, fabricated, or cross-tenant evidence_ref. Keep domain-separated signing tags; chain any new signed graph record to an owner-rooted segment, not a new un-rooted signer.

5) Tenant isolation. The graph must be scoped exactly like the spine: live under the per-tenant CRUCIBLE_ROOT (so assert_tenant_fleet_isolated covers it) OR carry tenant_id in every node key and every query predicate. The current Neo4j mirror's engagement_id-only partition is the cautionary example — do not copy it into a shared instance.

6) Authorization gates untouched. The graph authorizes NOTHING (integration rule 6: "the graph is inert"). conjunctive_decide, RBAC default-deny, the never-liftable egress floor, and the m-of-n destruction quorum remain SEPARATE conjuncts; a graph edge/coverage claim must never become an input that relaxes a gate (e.g. "the graph says in-scope" must not substitute for the per-request scope+egress re-authorization).

7) No secrets in any label/log/export. Run every graph label, node attr, and exported/rendered field through vigil_core.redact (mask by key-name) before it lands in a snapshot, log, or report — the WorldModel attrs bag and finding summaries can otherwise carry credential excerpts.

8) Append-only / provenance discipline. Preserve the blackboard's UPDATE/DELETE-refusal and bi-temporal 'never delete, set invalid_from' for retirements, so the investigation graph stays a replayable, byte-deterministic projection auditable back to the signed spine.

PRIVATE-MATRIX NOTE: this maps gaps in a PUBLIC repo; keep it in chat/~/.claude/plans. The design is independent (no ARTEX material consulted or referenced). Read-only audit — nothing was edited, written, or committed; no tools run against any target.

entity_coverage.exists: Rich and first-class, but split across TWO disjoint stores. worldmodel Node (HOST/SERVICE/ENDPOINT/WEBAPP/DATASTORE/CLOUD_RESOURCE/NETWORK_SEGMENT/PRINCIPAL/CREDENTIAL/SESSION/CONTROL + intel DOMAIN/CERTIFICATE/ASN/NETBLOCK/ORGANIZATION/PACKAGE/VULNERABILITY/...) each carrying a Beta belief + classify_provenance grounding tier; F4 recon-bridge nodes (Host/Port/Technology/Endpoint/CVE).
entity_coverage.gap: No shared asset-identity key between the two graphs: worldmodel ids are caller-assigned, F4 bridge ids are natural keys (host:<v>), so the belief-graph asset and the chain-graph asset that are the SAME host cannot be joined. The F4 bridge is a thin 5-label recon subset of the full asset kind-set. No tenant_id on either node (only engagement scope), so an asset id is cross-tenant-ambiguous in a shared CRUCIBLE_ROOT.

entity_coverage.exists: PARTIAL / implicit only. A goal appears solely as an attack-path DESTINATION: a worldmodel crown-jewel node whose kind is in pathsearch objective_kinds, and PathCertificate.destination. There is no declared-objective node.
entity_coverage.gap: No first-class Goal/Objective ENTITY bound to a charter objective. 'Goal' is node-kind membership, not an auditable, declared engagement objective that actions, leads and findings can be mapped to. The charter.md objectives never become a graph node, so coverage cannot be measured against stated objectives.

entity_coverage.exists: First-class. Spine event kinds (blackboard BlackboardEventRow.kind) + F4 ChainStep projected with STEP_TARGETED/EXPLOITED/IDENTIFIED and a tool prop; the raw-evidence directory is keyed by action_id.
entity_coverage.gap: action_id is a per-agent counter (A-NNN) or a content hash poc-<sha256(check_id)>, NOT an unguessable capability and NOT tenant-stamped. A ChainStep has no direct Action->Asset edge (it only reaches assets via the finding it PRODUCED) and no Action->Goal edge, so 'which action pursued which objective/asset' is not queryable.

entity_coverage.exists: First-class for positive/failure outcomes. F4 PRODUCED / FAILED_WITH edges, ChainFailure and ChainDecision nodes; the AUTHORITATIVE result is the signed oracle verdict (never the tool's word).
entity_coverage.gap: A benign/negative result ('tested, nothing found') is not represented as any node/edge, so the graph cannot distinguish 'not tested' from 'tested, no finding'. Result modeling is finding-biased; coverage of a surface that was probed cleanly is invisible.

entity_coverage.exists: First-class and strongly separated from facts. F4 ChainFinding with ConfirmationStatus.LEAD, agent Finding status=lead, worldmodel VULNERABILITY kind (threat-intel lead), confidence Evidence datum with Provenance.ref. Leads are physically unable to appear in confirmed_findings().
entity_coverage.gap: A lead's link to its verification ATTEMPT is not tracked. A lead never-yet-verified and a lead tested-but-not-confirmed look identical unless a grounded refute retired it, so 'which leads still await verification' is not answerable.

entity_coverage.exists: First-class and the strongest part of the system. EvidenceCertificate + verify_certificate re-fires the oracle over RETAINED bytes; reverify_context requires provenance in {reproduced,live_redrive}; projector._is_confirmed re-derives CONFIRMED; RemediationCertificate re-fires for the negative proof.
entity_coverage.gap: Verification is NOT dereferenced at the graph/query boundary. CONFIRMED derivation checks only that evidence_ref/signature_ref are NON-EMPTY; it never resolves+re-verifies the stored cert. There is NO evidence-by-ID resolver/index, so a dangling, mismatched, or cross-finding evidence_ref reads back as a FACT undetected. This is the central gap.

entity_coverage.exists: First-class across 4+ stores. EvidenceCertificate.finding_ref; F4 ChainFinding CONFIRMED (signed evidence_ref); worldmodel FINDING node + EVIDENCES edge; agent Finding type; human targets/<slug>/findings/NNN-*.md.
entity_coverage.gap: Finding identity is non-uniform (finding_ref slug vs spine_hash vs cert_digest vs NNN-slug.md vs worldmodel node id) with no canonical finding-key join. evidence_ref is an opaque, non-uniform string (detection cert_id | spine hash | SCITT/OpenVEX id | sha256:<digest>). No tenant_id on the EvidenceCertificate (engagement_slug only).

entity_coverage.exists: PARTIAL — certificate only, OFF-GRAPH. RemediationCertificate (vigil-remediation-cert-v2): a NEGATIVE proof earned by oracle silence over the patched build, binding original_finding_cert_digest -> the signed POSITIVE finding cert. reprove.py re-proves.
entity_coverage.gap: Remediation is a standalone signed JSON, NOT projected as a graph node/edge. The finding->remediation segment is invisible to the investigation graph; 'which confirmed findings have a remediation' cannot be answered by traversal, and nothing re-verifies the referenced finding cert at a graph boundary.

entity_coverage.exists: PARTIAL — signed ledger only, OFF-GRAPH. attestation_log.py VF-1b Continuous Attestation Log: a signed, hash-chained, anti-rollback monotonic series of 4-state prove-cert ticks (REMEDIATED/STILL_VULNERABLE/INCONCLUSIVE/REFUSED), each tick linked to its finding via the embedded remediation cert digest.
entity_coverage.gap: The retest ledger is rich but not projected as a first-class graph entity. The finding->remediation->retest lifecycle and its current status (Verified Fixed / Still Vulnerable / Inconclusive) is not queryable from the investigation/coverage graph; the retest.md status columns have to be assembled by hand from the ledger.

link_coverage.gap: A route is computed on demand and a PathCertificate binds it to a DESTINATION, but there is no persistent Asset->Goal edge keyed on a DECLARED objective node (goals are not entities). So 'which assets reach objective X' is a transient query, not a stored, auditable coverage link.

No goal entity and no Goal->Action / Action->Goal edge. 'Which actions pursued objective X', and 'which objectives have zero actions', are unanswerable. This is the single biggest missing adjacency in the chain.

link_coverage.store: integration/.../graph/model.py + projector.py (PRODUCED / FAILED_WITH, HAS_STEP / NEXT_STEP / LED_TO)
link_coverage.gap: Only positive/failure results are edged. A benign/negative result has no edge, so action->result coverage is finding-biased and cannot show a surface that was probed cleanly.

link_coverage.store: integration/.../graph/model.py (a ChainFinding LEAD produced by a step)
link_coverage.gap: Adequate. There is no explicit 'this later result supersedes/weakens that lead' beyond the refute mechanism, but the lead itself is well-represented.

link_coverage.store: integration/.../graph/projector.py (_is_confirmed, monotone LEAD->CONFIRMED on the same node) + evidence cert
link_coverage.gap: The link exists only as the successful upgrade. A verification ATTEMPT that did NOT confirm the lead is not recorded as an event linked to it (only a grounded refute retires it), and the evidence_ref is not dereferenced, so 'which leads have had a verification attempt' is not answerable.

link_coverage.store: engine/.../evidence/models.py (EvidenceCertificate.finding_ref) + integration/.../graph/projector.py (stamps evidence_ref on the node)
link_coverage.gap: Join by OPAQUE string, not a verified join. The graph never resolves evidence_ref -> SignedEvidence and re-checks finding_ref == the node's finding. A cert for finding A referenced on finding B's node, or a dangling ref, is undetected. No evidence-by-ID resolver exists.

A one-way digest inside a standalone JSON, not a graph edge. Nothing validates at a graph boundary that the referenced finding cert exists/verifies, and you cannot traverse finding->remediation in the investigation graph.

link_coverage.store: integration/.../remediation/attestation_log.py (ticks embed + re-execute the remediation cert; chained + anti-rollback)
link_coverage.gap: The retest series links to remediation (hence finding) by embedded cert digest, but as a separate signed ledger, not a graph edge. The lifecycle + current status is not queryable from the graph.

Two disjoint representations (worldmodel EVIDENCES vs F4 bridge) with no shared asset key; the F4 bridge covers only 5 recon labels, not the full worldmodel asset kind-set, so a finding on a DATASTORE/PRINCIPAL/CLOUD_RESOURCE has no F4 asset link.

THE central integrity gap: evidence_ref is never dereferenced or re-verified at the graph/query boundary (only checked non-empty). 'Evidence-linked' integrity is ASSUMED from the signed spine, not enforced by a join, so a dangling/mismatched/cross-tenant ref passes.
None material — this is the ONE link that IS join-verified (verify_bundle requires every backing cert present AND itself verified, fail-closed). It is the exact model the other links should copy.

acceptance_tests: Flag OFF: graph.query public API is byte-identical to pre-slice; no coverage function is exposed.
Flag ON: coverage(view) reports, per Goal, the count of Actions that PURSUE it and whether any confirmed Finding AFFECTS an asset that REACHES it; a Goal with zero actions is surfaced as uncovered.

Honesty invariant: an asset/surface with no finding is reported as not_tested UNLESS a benign/negative result record exists for it, in which case tested_no_finding — silence is NEVER reported as CLEAN/safe.

Flag ON: per confirmed Finding, coverage reports remediation present|absent and retest verified_fixed|still_vulnerable|inconclusive|none, derived only from JOIN-verified (S2/S4) nodes — an unverified remediation never shows as verified_fixed.
Flag ON: a LEAD finding is reported under leads_unverified and never under findings_confirmed (the lead/fact split carries into coverage).
Flag ON: coverage counts only ACTIVE (non-retired) nodes — a refuted lead drops from the unverified-leads count (bi-temporal honored).
Non-authoritative: the coverage result is stamped retrieval_only=True / authoritative=False — it grants nothing and authorizes no action.
Determinism: coverage(view) is a pure function of the view — same view yields byte-identical, sorted coverage JSON; no wallclock.
No secrets: every label/count in the coverage export passes the F3 redactor — no host/credential/token leaks into a coverage label.

Fail-closed honesty on sparse data: with an empty/partial graph, coverage never crashes and never reports 100%/CLEAN for an un-scanned goal — missing data reads as unknown/not_tested, never as covered.

safety_preserved: FACT-minting authority unchanged and only ever tightened: CONFIRMED is still RE-DERIVED from an oracle-signed, re-executing evidence cert (projector._is_confirmed + the S2 join), never from a producer/LLM/planner claim. The join can only DEMOTE — the ON set of confirmed findings is always a subset of OFF; no slice adds a promote/grant/tier path.

Planner/consumer cannot read authority from the graph: every read stays retrieval_only=True / authoritative=False and FROZEN (PriorChainContext); leads never leak into the confirmed set; Goal/Remediation/Retest nodes are inert and excluded from confirmed_findings().

'Nothing found' is never CLEAN: coverage distinguishes not_tested from tested_no_finding (needs a real benign/negative observation); refutation RETIRES bi-temporally (invalid_from), never deletes; a non-oracle-grounded refute can retire only a LEAD and stays resurrectable.

Evidence integrity/signing preserved and strengthened: every resolved cert is re-verified by the EXISTING re-execution path (m-of-n Ed25519 + trust-root fingerprint pin + artifact sha256 re-hash + chain / monotonic anti-rollback highwater); a dangling, mismatched, tampered, or cross-finding evidence_ref fails CLOSED and can no longer read back as a FACT.

Tenant isolation: every new node/edge/resolver is tenant+engagement-scoped; a cross-tenant or fabricated evidence ID is rejected at resolve (S1) and at the join (S2); the one-root-per-tenant requirement and assert_tenant_fleet_isolated are untouched; no cross-engagement cert reuse.

Additive / byte-identical OFF: every slice is default-OFF behind its own VIGIL_* flag and, with the flag off (and, for the pure-projection slices, even on for a spine carrying no new records), serialises byte-identically — no existing signature, cert digest, spine record, or golden snapshot changes.

Determinism + rebuildable: every projection remains a pure function of the signed spine (plus already-signed certs/ticks), ordered by spine seq, with no wallclock/RNG — the read-model stays independently rebuildable and verifiable, never a parallel source of truth.

No offensive capability added: every slice is read-model or verification-tightening only; none issues traffic, runs a live oracle/retest, or adds a tool/exec/egress symbol; all re-execution is over RETAINED bytes via the existing verify path (enforced by a per-PR symbol grep guard).

No secrets in labels/logs/exports: every new label/prop/coverage field passes the existing F3 redactor; private keys stay in process memory; no credential/host/token enters a graph label or coverage export.
gap_matrix.rationale: Do NOT introduce a new graph database; extend the existing stores. All nine gaps are missing PROJECTIONS and JOINS over data that is already the single signed source of truth (the hash-chained, dual-Ed25519-signed event spine), not a missing storage engine. The F4 GraphView is already a deterministic, rebuildable read-model projected one-way from that spine by a single writer (graph/projector.py), and an optional real Neo4j binder already exists behind VIGIL_GRAPH_BACKEND=neo4j, written only by rebuild_from_spine. The target investigation+coverage graph is small (per-engagement: hundreds to low-thousands of nodes) and every query these slices need — 1-3 hop lifecycle traversal (finding->remediation->retest), asset/goal coverage rollups, evidence-ref joins — is satisfied comfortably by the in-memory GraphView or the existing Neo4j projection. A new DB would be actively harmful here: it would create a SECOND source of truth (the exact trust-laundering risk the projector was built to prevent), add an unsigned write path outside the spine, and multiply the tenant-isolation surface (another store that would need the one-root-per-tenant guarantee). The sound architecture is to keep the spine as the only source of truth and add: (S1) an evidence-by-ID resolver that merely indexes certs already on disk; (S2) a join that dereferences+re-verifies evidence_ref before CONFIRMED (closing the central 'non-empty != verified' gap, demote-only so FACT authority can only tighten); (S3) a declared Goal/Objective node; (S4) projection of the existing RemediationCertificate + attestation_log ticks into finding->remediation->retest nodes/edges; and (S5) a non-authoritative coverage rollup. Each is one additive, default-OFF, byte-identical-when-off PR extending a named existing module (evidence/, graph/model.py, graph/projector.py, graph/query.py), expanding no offensive capability. A new DB should be reconsidered ONLY on a measured requirement that the in-memory view and Neo4j binder provably cannot meet — e.g. cross-engagement analytics over millions of nodes or sub-100ms multi-hop queries at that scale — none of which is present in this single-engagement, audit-first model. Note on the relayed 'build everything in parallel' intent: S1 and S3 have no dependencies and can be built concurrently; S2 and S4 each depend only on S1 (parallel to each other); S5 depends on S2+S3+S4 and lands last. This step itself is the READ-ONLY design deliverable — no files were written, ARTEX was not opened, and the matrix is intended to stay private (chat / ~/.claude/plans), never the public tree.
